reasoning: The brief is a two-figure swap over the attached video: 'swap them both' with two replacement images supplied. Caller wiring pins <Picture 1> to the bearded man in the plaid shirt (<Subject 3>). <Picture 2> carries no explicit target in the manifest, but the stated intent names both people in the clip, so it resolves semantically to the only other person observed there, the young woman at the lathe (<Subject 4>). The replacement portraits are identity plates, not anchored frames: their grey studio backdrop, even lighting and full-body posing are presentation and must not be carried into the workshop. The wood-panelled workshop with multi-paned windows, daylight, hammer, workbench and lathe all come from the source video and stay; only the two people's identities change, preserving the source motion (hammer raised and struck, then turning to camera) and the tightening framing. Coverage of the video is partial (3 sampled frames), so only the described action is claimed; camera move is a small, slow push in per the observed tightening. Dialogue and visible text were not requested, so speech, onscreen text and lettering stay empty; no explicit prohibitions were stated. Balanced creativity permits a subtle score, but the caller asked only for the swap, so none is added. Single cut, continuous take, matching the ~5.2s target duration.

shots.action: In the wood-panelled workshop, the elderly woman in the bright yellow raincoat — her short white hair and build taken from <Picture 1> — now stands where the bearded man in the plaid shirt was, driving a nail at the workbench: she raises the hammer and strikes, then turns her head toward the camera. Behind her at the lathe, the young man in the blue coat from <Picture 2> has taken the place of the young woman in the grey apron, steadying his hands on the work and glancing up. Daylight from the large multi-paned windows keeps the same fall and direction, and the plate portraits' grey studio backdrop is nowhere present.

shots.what_changes: Both people in the workshop are replaced by the new figures while the hammer strike and turn toward camera play out and the framing slowly tightens
